research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Is the reorganization measure defined and reliable (split-half or test-retest) before it is correlated with PPP change?
Do 148 spells (n=986 units) give enough power for a correlation-type test at the minimum detectable effect?
Is the PPP-change outcome independent of the play-by-play used to build the reorganization measure?
How are regression to the mean, selection on extreme absences, lineup, opponent, and playoff-vs-regular-season context handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Team-season defensive H2-adjustment reliability. Split-half r=-0.001 for the H2-change trait, with p<.05 needing about r=0.18 on 120 team-seasons. The H1 defensive level r=+0.356 showed the test pipeline works. Season-to-season values were -0.19, -0.26, +0.16. Offensive H2-change r=+0.139 was not significant. Recorded limitation: LIM:low_measurement_reliability; risks MEASURE_RELIABILITY and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

Final checks on defensive H2-adjustment trait reliability, a Design 5 placebo, and a start-of-half dip. Method was split-half (odd/even game) reliability of team-season H2-H1 change. Verdict recorded as inconclusive. Observed result NOT_RECORDED; no log saved. Confidence low (0.15).

Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games across 55 series, 179 players, 25 teams, minimum 10 possessions per player. Descriptive only. Team AVOID% ranged from 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC). Team BEST% ranged from 0.0% to 15.8%. No outcome test was run.

Regular-season vs playoff PPP by play type. DRIVE PPP was 1.198 in the regular season and 0.912 in the playoffs (-0.286, 25 teams). PNR was -0.173 and PULL_UP +0.301; other types were within -0.07. Minimum 30 possessions per cell, no confidence intervals reported. Verdict supported, with the result motivating a playoff DRIVE exclusion.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a reliable trait (team-level defensive second-half adjustment) by split-half correlation of a change score.
failed_approaches.why: Split-half r=-0.001 against a detectable threshold of about 0.18 on 120 team-seasons. Recorded as untestable (A_unanswerable) because of low measurement reliability.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Split-half reliability of team-season H2-H1 change, plus a placebo check on triggered vs non-triggered units.
failed_approaches.why: No result or log saved; mechanism recorded as E_unclear. Verdict inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: Change-score measures built from split halves of a season were not reliable in the closest retrieved analogue (SF-CHT-064): the reliability correlation was near zero and far below the detectable threshold.
The retrieved pipelines can recover a strong known relation (H1 defensive level r=+0.356 in SF-CHT-064), so a validated check against a known effect is feasible.
Playoff and regular-season PPP differ by play type in the one retrieved study (SF-APPS-011, DRIVE -0.286), so game context is a plausible confounder for PPP-based outcomes.
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests player absence, offensive reorganization relative to L, or their link to PPP change. All retrieved records are on defensive H2 adjustment, trigger tables, or play-type PPP.
No record defines the reorganization metric or the baseline L, and the task statement does not define them either.
The sample sizes and power for the present question are not established by any retrieved record. The units (n=986 and 148 spells) and the phrase 'mde rho' are not explained in any record.
No retrieved record reports a reliability estimate for an offensive reorganization measure.
own_inferences: With 148 spells, a two-sided test at alpha 0.05 and 80% power detects |r| of about 0.23 (my own approximation, not a recorded result). Effects of the size seen in the analogue studies would be undetectable at that n.
The outcome (PPP change) and the reorganization measure would both come from the same play-by-play. Any shared possessions or shared event definitions would inflate the association mechanically.
Spells selected on extreme absences would show regression to the mean in PPP change, which could produce a spurious association with any measure correlated with baseline PPP.
Because the question is stated as a correlation with no direction or threshold, a 'supported' result would be easy to produce with post-hoc specification choices.
uncertainties: The definition of L and of the reorganization index is missing.
Whether 'n=986 units' means possessions, games, or player-games is unknown, and so is the meaning of 'mde rho'.
Playoff 2025-26 data were partial before 2026-06-21; the freeze date for the analysis is not stated.
Whether the derived play-type graph records are independent of the PPP outcome is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The closest analogue (SF-CHT-064) was recorded as untestable because its change-score reliability was near zero, and SF-TMP-005 produced no result. Their pattern suggests that a change-score measure built on this data may not be reliable enough to test a correlation. That moved the decision from proceed-with-design to do_not_proceed until reliability of the reorganization measure is shown. This is an inference from analogue records, not a finding about the present question.

blocking_constraints.text: The reorganization measure and its change-score structure have no recorded reliability; the closest analogue had split-half r near zero.
With 148 spells, power is limited to moderate correlations (about |r|≥0.23 by my approximation); the stated MDE is not interpretable without a defined rho.
PPP change and the reorganization measure are both derived from the same play-by-play, so the outcome is not independent of the predictor.
Spells are selected on absence, so regression to the mean in PPP change is expected unless a baseline-adjusted design is used.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses player absence, offensive reorganization relative to L, or their association with PPP change. The closest records concern team-level defensive H2 adjustment reliability (untestable, reliability near zero), a related reliability check with no result recorded, and regular-season vs playoff PPP by play type (supported, DRIVE gap). They inform reliability and context-confounding risks only.

risks.text: Reorganization and change-score measures have no reliability estimate; the analogue change score had split-half r near zero.
148 spells give limited power for moderate correlations; stated MDE rho is undefined.
PPP change is derived from the same play-by-play as the reorganization measure.
Play-type and initiator labels come from a derived graph; misclassified possessions would bias both measures.
Selection on extreme absences produces regression to the mean in PPP change.
Lineup, opponent, minutes, and playoff vs regular-season context can drive both reorganization and PPP change (SF-APPS-011 shows a large playoff DRIVE gap).
Using post-absence possessions to define reorganization or the baseline would leak the outcome.
Spells with few possessions per play type would give unstable PPP and reorganization estimates.
Choice among many reorganization definitions, windows, and baselines L inflates false positives.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 playoff data differ in pace and rules; pooling may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Within-spell association (Pearson r and regression slope with 95% CI) between a pre-registered offensive reorganization index relative to baseline L and the change in PPP from baseline to post-absence windows.
design.unit: Player-absence spell (one row per spell); possessions aggregated within spell windows.
design.sample: Clarify the 986 units and 148 spells first. Use complete regular-season files 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 RS complete from 2026-04-13); exclude partial 2025-26 playoff data. Freeze the data version at 2026-11-01.
design.power: Compute before analysis. Own approximation: 80% power at alpha 0.05 two-sided for |r|≈0.23 with n=148 spells. Smaller effects are not detectable; report that the test is underpowered for them.
design.controls: Pre-absence baseline PPP and reorganization; lineup and minutes; opponent strength; home/away; playoff indicator; cluster-robust errors by team-season. Define L and the reorganization window before outcome data are used. Use only pre-absence and absence-window events for both measures to avoid lookahead.
design.falsification: Placebo spells (matched non-absence games with the same reorganization computation) should show no association. A split-half or test-retest reliability of the reorganization index must reach a pre-registered threshold before the primary test is interpreted. Outcome-independence check: recompute the measure from a disjoint possession set.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification (pre-registered L, window, and index). Secondary specifications reported as exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary CI excludes zero, placebo spells are null, reliability meets the threshold, and the result holds under the disjoint-possession check. Rejected only if the test is adequately powered for the pre-registered effect and the CI is tight around zero. Otherwise report uncertain or untestable.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as listed; 2025-26 playoffs only from complete files (2026-06-21 onward); analysis frozen at 2026-11-01.

methodological_questions: Is the sample of 148 spells (n=986 units) sufficient to detect the minimum detectable effect in a correlation between reorganization and change in points per possession?
How should offensive reorganization be measured reliably from play-by-play and play-type data?
How can regression to the mean and selection on extreme absence spells be handled?
What confounders (lineup, opponent, game context, playoff vs regular season) affect the reorganization to points-per-possession association?
Does the outcome definition risk being derived from the same play-by-play used to measure reorganization?
args.query: player absence offensive reorganization change in points per possession relative to baseline L, spell-level analysis, minimum detectable effect, measurement reliability, NBA play-by-play

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
